title: Balance-sniffing accounting in _syncBudget and topUp is fragile against non-canonical reward-token transfer semantics and external donations
regression-risk: pre-existing (prior CS-04, unaddressed); ES-07 adds donation-inflation angle
description:
Three accounting sites rely on raw `balanceOf(this)` without a tracked-balance variable, creating compounding drift opportunities:

1. `_syncBudget` (lines 212-216): `inflow = balanceOf(this) - pre`, crediting the delta. If the reward token has non-standard transfer semantics (fee-on-transfer, rebasing, blacklist, mint-with-fee), the dispatcher's view of 'debt cleared' diverges from the staker's `rewardBudget`.

2. `topUp` (line 189-190): credits the full input `amount`, with NO before/after balance measurement — so a fee-on-transfer token causes `rewardBudget` to exceed the true balance. Under the story-002 `_safePay` revert semantics, the eventual consequence is that later claims revert on 'insufficient reward balance' instead of silently forfeiting — user-visible breakage rather than silent loss, but users are blocked from accounting-entitled rewards until owner tops up the gap.

3. External donations (ES-07 angle): anyone can `rewardToken.transfer` directly to the contract. The donation is NOT credited to `rewardBudget`, but it IS visible to `_safePay` (passes the balance check) and to `totalDebt()` (which computes `balance - budget`). `totalDebt` over-reports by the donation size, misleading off-chain dashboards; `_safePay` may spend donations as an accidental buffer for accumulated truncation dust; and the donated funds are stranded after window end unless owner reconfigures.

The contract spec states phUSD is a vanilla ERC20, making the FoT/rebasing path a defensive-coding concern. The donation-inflation path is an observable mis-accounting regardless of token behavior.
impact: (a) If phUSD ever has non-canonical transfer semantics: `topUp` over-credits budget; later claims revert on shortfall and users are blocked until manual owner top-up fills the gap. (b) `totalDebt()` view is inflated by any donated funds; monitors and UIs that display 'unpaid rewards' misreport. (c) Donated funds become an opaque payment buffer consumed by `_safePay` for rounding/truncation overages, and are non-refundable to the donor. No direct value-leak to stakers, but accounting invariants drift and monitoring becomes unreliable.
proof:
FoT example: owner calls `topUp(100e18)` with a 1% FoT token; `safeTransferFrom` delivers 99e18; `rewardBudget += 100e18`. After emission, users try to claim pro-rata totalling 100e18 but balance is only 99e18 — last claimants revert on `_safePay`. They cannot claim until another top-up closes the 1e18 gap.

Donation example: adversary transfers Y phUSD directly to the NFTStaker contract. `totalDebt()` immediately reports `+Y`. Off-chain 'unpaid rewards' monitors alert spuriously. Y is stranded after window end unless owner calls `setWindowDuration` (which has its own mintDebt-exclusion issue — see F-03) or is slowly consumed as a buffer for truncation overages.
suggested-fix: Introduce an `accountedBalance` storage variable updated at every credit/debit site, and replace `rewardToken.balanceOf(this)` in `_safePay` and `totalDebt` with the tracked value. For `topUp`: snapshot `balanceOf` before and after `safeTransferFrom`, credit the delta. For `_syncBudget`: have `dispatcherHook.pull()` RETURN the amount credited, and use that instead of balance-sniffing (eliminates both the FoT drift and the reentrancy-delta concern from F-06). Add a dedicated `donate()` entrypoint that adds transferred amount to `rewardBudget` and emits an event, giving donors a predictable path. Document the canonical-ERC20 assumption in NatSpec.
consolidation-note: CS-04 (FoT/rebasing concern) and ES-07 (external donation inflating totalDebt) share the same root cause — balance-sniffing instead of a tracked balance. Merged because the fix (tracked `accountedBalance`) resolves both. Each sub-concern preserved.
